title: Title & Registration Services Policy Manual, Clause on Relief for Repeated State Returns of a Fee-Shortage Order
content:
**Clause.** Kestrel relieves part of a Title & Registration Services buyer's fee-shortage cure payment for the times the state has sent the order back: one fifth (0.20) when the order carries three or more returns, one tenth (0.10) when it carries exactly two, and nothing when it carries fewer.

**Counting.** The returns counted are all state rejection entries on the title order, whatever their reason, including the fee-shortage return itself.

**Application.** The relief is a fraction of the cure payment as it stands before any relief is taken off, and that fraction of it is taken off the payment; the result is rounded half up to the cent only at the end.

## The clause at each count

| State returns on the order | Relief |
|---|---|
| 1 | nothing |
| 2 | one tenth (0.10) |
| 3 | one fifth (0.20) |
| 4 or more | one fifth (0.20) |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- An order returned once for a missing signature and later once for a fee shortage carries two returns: the relief is one tenth, so a cure payment of 40.00 before relief becomes 36.00.
- An order returned once only, for the fee shortage, receives no relief under this clause.
